From Molecules to Mind — Timeline

No single “cause” flips molecules into mind. Instead, stacked emergences — replication, signaling, neural integration, social cognition — yield systems capable of subjective experience and culture.

This timeline sketches a plausible pathway from prebiotic chemistry to emergent mind, combining views from neuroscience, Buddhist philosophy, and physics/complexity. It does not assert a single cause; rather, it shows staged emergence where new properties arise from interactions at each level.

Each stage adds new interactions and constraints. Mind is framed as an emergent system-level property once information integration and differentiation reach sufficient complexity.

Lens Key Idea Memory Relevance Comment
Neuroscience Global broadcasting & integration (e.g., Global Workspace); information structure (IIT) Hippocampus binds scenes; cortex stores features; reconstruction at recall Conscious access depends on network-level dynamics
Buddhism Dependent origination: mental events arise with conditions; no fixed self Memory as constructed process; clinging to narratives increases suffering Focus on training attention/ethics to alter arising patterns
Physics/Complexity Emergence: macro-laws from micro-interactions; phase transitions Qualitative shifts when connectivity crosses thresholds Analogous to temperature or turbulence emerging from particles

References

  • Koch, C. (2019). The Feeling of Life Itself: Why Consciousness Is Widespread but Can’t Be Computed. MIT Press.
  • Maynard Smith, J., & Szathmáry, E. (1995). The Major Transitions in Evolution. Oxford University Press.
  • Varela, F. J., Thompson, E., & Rosch, E. (1991). The Embodied Mind: Cognitive Science and Human Experience. MIT Press.
